requirement:
{impl}`requirements.configuration.feature_sections`
`--config <name>` MUST select a configuration for that invocation. Otherwise,
authoring MUST use the user's selection for the canonical project root, then the
workspace default, then the user's default. Named workspace configurations MUST
override same-named user configurations as complete records. Backend, model,
connection settings, and options MUST come from the selected record as a unit;
fields MUST NOT be merged between records. Workspace-only authoring MUST work
without a user configuration file. Missing configuration or an unknown selection
MUST identify the relevant configuration file and point to documented examples.

An explicit Bedrock AWS profile or region MUST override the corresponding SDK
default; omitted values MUST use standard AWS SDK resolution. Ollama MUST use
its configured endpoint or `http://localhost:11434`. If `api_key_env` is set, its
named variable MUST supply the credential; a missing or empty value MUST produce
an error before a model request. OpenAI MUST use its configured endpoint or
`https://api.openai.com/v1`, and MUST resolve `OPENAI_API_KEY` when neither
`api_key` nor `api_key_env` is supplied.
rationale:
The marked tests cover every obligation in `requirements.authoring.configuration_precedence`.

**Selection order and `--config`**
- `tests/configuration.rs#fn[explicit_project_and_default_selections_choose_whole_configs]` asserts three things. The user default is chosen when nothing else applies. A project selection is chosen once one exists for the root, and the root is passed as `root.join(".")`, so canonicalisation is exercised. An explicit name wins over both the project selection and the default.
- `tests/configuration.rs#fn[workspace_defaults_and_configs_combine_with_existing_user_selections]` covers the rest of the order. A workspace default beats the user default. A user project selection beats the workspace default. A workspace default naming a user config resolves to the user record. The user default is used when the workspace has no default. The explicit name `workspace` is selected even though a project selection exists.

**Whole-record override and no merging**
- In `workspace_defaults_and_configs_combine_with_existing_user_selections`, the workspace `shared` config replaces the user one. The user record has a bedrock backend, concurrency 7 and temperature/top_p options. The resolved record has a model of `replacement`, no endpoint, concurrency `None` and options of only `{temperature: 0.8}`.
- `tests/configuration.rs#fn[workspace_configurations_accept_validate_and_override_concurrency]` shows that concurrency from the user record does not leak through, for all three backends.

**Workspace-only operation**
- `tests/configuration.rs#fn[workspace_defaults_and_configs_combine_with_existing_user_selections]` resolves with no user config.
- `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[authoring_uses_nearest_workspace_configuration_without_a_user_file]` runs the CLI end to end with the user file deleted. It checks the model and the credential on the wire, and that no user file is created.

**Missing configuration and unknown selection**
- `explicit_project_and_default_selections_choose_whole_configs` asserts that an unknown name or missing configuration yields an error naming `config.toml` and the `editing-the-file` documentation anchor.
- `tests/configuration.rs#fn[unknown_selections_name_the_file_that_made_them]` covers a dangling user default, a dangling project selection and a dangling workspace default. It also covers an unknown `--config` name searched in both files, and the case with no workspace file.
- `tests/configuration.rs#fn[configurations_without_any_selection_report_how_to_choose_one]` covers configurations that exist but are not selected.

**Bedrock**
- `src/authoring/providers.rs#mod[tests]/fn[omitted_bedrock_profile_and_region_use_standard_sdk_resolution]` shows that omitted values match plain SDK resolution. It also shows that an explicit profile resolves as the SDK would and that an explicit region overrides the profile's region.
- `explicit_bedrock_credentials_reach_the_sdk_without_the_default_chain` checks explicit credentials and region.
- `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[bedrock_cli_uses_selected_profile_region_and_converse_tools]` is an end-to-end test. A profile and region are set against a wrong default profile, and the SigV4 credential and region on the wire are asserted.
- `all_adapters_preserve_prompt_tools_and_evidence_with_default_connections` covers the default chain when neither value is given. It asserts the environment key and the `ap-south-1` region.

**Ollama and OpenAI**
- `backend_configuration_round_trips_without_materializing_defaults` asserts the Ollama default endpoint `http://localhost:11434`. `tests/configuration.rs#fn[openai_configuration_preserves_model_and_resolves_credentials]` asserts the OpenAI default endpoint `https://api.openai.com/v1`. It also asserts that `OPENAI_API_KEY` is the variable read when neither `api_key` nor `api_key_env` is set, and that a custom endpoint is used.
- `tests/configuration.rs#fn[ollama_authentication_resolves_separately_and_rejects_missing_values]` and the OpenAI test show that a missing or empty `api_key_env` value is an error. A set value is returned.
- `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[missing_or_empty_api_key_env_fails_before_any_model_request]` runs the CLI for ollama and openai with the variable unset and empty. It asserts a failure naming the variable and no connection to the listener.
- `all_adapters_preserve_prompt_tools_and_evidence_with_default_connections` and `openai_responses_replays_tool_calls_and_records_usage` check the configured endpoints and keys on the wire.

**Minor observation, not a gap**
`tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[an_explicit_configuration_selects_the_nondefault_workspace_profile]` is the CLI-level test of the `--config` flag. It carries `{test}` references to `requirements.authoring.invocation` and `requirements.authoring.configuration`, but none to this requirement. The flag only passes the name to the resolver. The selection semantics are covered by the marked resolver tests above, so I treat this as not an adequacy gap.
